scope: Exact-hash read-only review of unselected source4648 lesson; no draft, source-decision, selected-manifest, media or release edits.

source.meaning: Allows firms to continue operating; a life metaphor.

ownerComparison.owner349Meaning: Continue operating or meet basic financial demands despite difficulty.
ownerComparison.judgment: Potentially distinct causative keep-X-alive construction versus stative stay-afloat, but most current assessed decisions duplicate owner349’s basic-cost survival versus expansion distinction. A separate lesson needs substantially different causal/evidence/transfer decisions.

findings.finding: Six of seven stages repeatedly present a business with income exactly covering essential rent/wages, then contrast survival with expansion. The setting names change, but the learner repeatedly makes the same decision already central to owner349 stay afloat. The lesson does not yet demonstrate seven materially different uses of the causative keep-X-alive construction.
findings.repair: Keep the source meaning but diversify the communicative decisions: e.g. one stage attributes survival to a source of demand, another tests whether public attention is enough evidence, another handles temporary support versus future viability, another explains dependence on one contract, and final writing transfers to a genuinely different causal decision. Avoid repeating the same rent/wages/no-expansion frame in every step.

findings.finding: The prompt asks how to explain the order’s value to the partner. Option C mainly proposes thanking the office and reviewing next month; option D says when the order matters but omits that it pays remaining essential costs. Neither independently explains the established current value as clearly as A/B, weakening the four-valid-reply contract.
findings.repair: Make C and D independently answer what the order currently does for the café in EN/ZH, while preserving distinct natural phrasing and one target-bearing golden option; alternatively broaden the prompt to ask for both an explanation and sensible next action, then recheck every option.

findings.finding: The scene calls the venue a community theatre, but the keyed line recasts it as “the business” / 「這間企業」. A community theatre may be a non-profit organisation, so the referent sounds forced and distracts from the target.
findings.repair: Use an explicitly commercial venue in the prompt, or teach a natural theatre/company target form with bounded detector and aligned Chinese; keep the cost and future-risk facts grounded.

findings.finding: Model 2 distinguishes survival from growth but omits the prompt/self-check’s concrete statement that no money remains for expansion. Model 1 supplies it; both models are required to satisfy the same prompt.
findings.repair: Add the owner’s no-surplus-for-expansion fact in both languages and regenerate any shifted glossary spans.

verdict: Hold draft unselected pending scoped repair and independent exact-hash follow-up.
